caption: Figure 1: Comparison of the scores obtained for GPT-4o, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Phi-3-small using transcripts with varied levels of noise on the test set of ELITR-Bench-QA in single-turn mode. Indicated levels of noise correspond to the target Word Error Rates set in our noise injection procedure.

Figure 2: (a) Distribution of GPT-4 and Silver Human scores with respect to each Gold Human score bin (1-10); the N below a score bin indicates the bin size. (b) Pearson correlation between evaluators.

Figure 3: Results restricted to QA/Conv differentiating questions. The score reported for each model and evaluation setting corresponds to the average of the scores obtained on the dev subset (16 questions) and the test subset (17 questions). Best viewed in color.
Figure 4: Interface for our Prolific crowdsourcing study to collect Silver Human score annotations.

Figure6: Evaluation prompt for the GPT-4 evaluator, inspired from Kim et al.<ref type="bibr" target="#b22">[23]</ref>. The elements in blue and enclosed in curly brackets correspond to question-specific text spans that are dynamically adapted.
Figure7: Score rubric for the GPT-4 evaluator. Boldface is added for the sake of readability and is not included in the actual prompt.

Answer prompt used to obtain LLMs' responses. Questions are appended to this prompt as described in Section 4. The element in blue and enclosed in curly brackets corresponds to a meeting-specific text span that is dynamically adapted.
